title: 30-Minute Modeling Sprint
summary: Model one recognisable object in half an hour, then stop.
description: Set a timer for thirty minutes and model one everyday object: a mug, a hammer, a chair. When the timer ends you stop, finished or not. Speed work teaches you which details actually matter.
deliverables: A screenshot of whatever you had when the timer went off.
victoryConditions: You set a timer and stopped modelling when it ended.
The object is recognisable to someone who did not watch you build it.
stretchGoals: Run the sprint again on the same object and compare the two.
reflectionPrompt: Which detail did you spend too long on for how much it mattered?

title: Hotkey Hunter
summary: Replace five mouse trips with five keyboard shortcuts.
description: Pick five actions you currently do by hunting through menus, learn their shortcuts, and use them exclusively for one editing session. Speed is not vanity; it is the difference between trying an idea and skipping it.
deliverables: A written list of the five shortcuts you drilled.
victoryConditions: You listed five actions you normally reach for with the mouse.
You completed one full session using the shortcuts instead of the menus.
stretchGoals: Add five more and drill them tomorrow.
reflectionPrompt: Which shortcut already feels automatic, and which one still needs thinking?

title: Three-Cut Story
summary: Tell something complete using exactly three shots.
description: Three shots, no more. Set up a situation, turn it, and end it. The constraint forces every shot to do real work, which is the whole point.
deliverables: An exported clip made of exactly three shots.
victoryConditions: The finished clip contains exactly three shots and no more.
Someone watching it can say what happened without being told.
stretchGoals: Do it again with three completely different shots.
reflectionPrompt: Which of the three shots was carrying the most weight?

title: Camera Copycat
summary: Recreate a shot you admire, frame for frame.
description: Pick a single shot from something you like and rebuild it: the framing, the lens feel, the height, the movement. Copying carefully teaches more about camera decisions than reading about them ever will.
deliverables: Your recreation next to a still of the original.
victoryConditions: You placed your version and the reference side by side for comparison.
You matched the framing and the approximate camera height of the original.
stretchGoals: Write down the one difference you could not reproduce and why.
reflectionPrompt: What decision in the original did you only notice once you tried to copy it?

title: Transition Blacksmith
summary: Build three transitions that serve the cut instead of decorating it.
description: Most transitions are wallpaper. Build three that actually mean something: a match cut, a sound-led transition, and one motivated by movement. Then defend each one in a sentence.
deliverables: A clip showing three different motivated transitions.
victoryConditions: You built three distinct transitions, each of a different kind.
You wrote one sentence defending why each transition belongs there.
stretchGoals: Remove the weakest one and see whether the cut improves.
reflectionPrompt: Which transition would still work if you deleted the effect entirely?

title: Foley Goblin
summary: Record five sounds with household objects and sync them to picture.
description: Go make noise. Record five foley sounds using whatever is around you, then place them against picture so they read as the thing on screen rather than the thing in your kitchen.
deliverables: A clip with five self-recorded foley sounds in sync.
victoryConditions: You recorded five sounds yourself rather than downloading them.
Each sound lands in sync with the action it is meant to belong to.
stretchGoals: Layer two recordings into one convincing sound.
reflectionPrompt: Which household object made the least likely but most convincing sound?

title: Light Puzzle
summary: Light one subject three ways and name what each lighting says.
description: Same subject, same camera, three lighting setups: friendly, neutral, threatening. Nothing else changes. This is the fastest way to learn that lighting is meaning, not brightness.
deliverables: Three renders or photos of one subject under three lighting setups.
victoryConditions: Only the lighting changed between the three images.
You wrote down what each setup makes the subject feel like.
stretchGoals: Achieve the threatening version using only one light.
reflectionPrompt: Which setup changed the subject most with the smallest change in lights?

title: Material Duel
summary: Build the same surface twice and keep the one that survives scrutiny.
description: Pick a surface, worn metal, wet stone, old leather, and author it twice with different approaches. Render both under identical light and judge them side by side. Keep the winner, note why it won.
deliverables: A side-by-side render of two versions of the same surface.
victoryConditions: Both versions were rendered under identical lighting conditions.
You wrote down which one won and the reason it won.
stretchGoals: Rebuild the loser using what made the winner work.
reflectionPrompt: Was the difference in the texture maps or in the shading setup?

title: Graph Editor Gym
summary: Fix a bad animation using curves only, without adding keys.
description: Take a piece of stiff animation and improve it entirely in the Graph Editor. No new keyframes allowed. You will learn that most bad animation is a spacing problem wearing a timing costume.
deliverables: Before and after playback of the same animation.
victoryConditions: You improved the motion without adding a single new keyframe.
You captured a before and after recording for comparison.
stretchGoals: Do it again on a different clip with only two curve handles moved.
reflectionPrompt: Which curve change made the biggest difference to how it felt?

title: Loop Arena
summary: Build a seamless animated loop with no visible seam.
description: Loops are unforgiving: any mistake repeats forever. Animate something cyclical and make the last frame hand over to the first without a jump. Watch it ten times before you call it done.
deliverables: A looping render that plays at least three cycles.
victoryConditions: The loop plays three full cycles with no visible jump at the seam.
You watched it repeatedly at full speed before declaring it finished.
stretchGoals: Add a second element looping at a different rate.
reflectionPrompt: Where did the seam show first, and what fixed it?

title: Texture Detective
summary: Study a real surface closely, then reproduce what you actually saw.
description: Photograph a real surface up close. List what you genuinely observe: the scratches, the grime in the recesses, the way it changes at the edges. Then build it. Observation first, node graph second.
deliverables: Your reference photo, your observation list, and your render.
victoryConditions: You wrote the observation list before building anything.
Your render reproduces at least three specific details from the list.
stretchGoals: Show both to someone and ask which one is the photograph.
reflectionPrompt: Which detail did you only notice because you wrote the list first?

title: Environment Microstory
summary: Tell a story with an empty room and no people in it.
description: Build or photograph a space that implies something happened, and let the props do the talking. No characters, no text, no narration. If a viewer invents a story, it worked.
deliverables: One image of an empty space that implies an event.
victoryConditions: The image contains no people and no explanatory text.
Someone else looked at it and told you a story about what happened.
stretchGoals: Remove one prop and check whether the story still reads.
reflectionPrompt: Which object did the most storytelling work in the frame?

title: Pose Sheet
summary: Draw or block five poses that read clearly in silhouette.
description: Pose five distinct attitudes and test each one as a solid black silhouette. If you cannot tell them apart in silhouette, the pose is not clear yet, no matter how good the details are.
deliverables: Five poses shown both normally and as silhouettes.
victoryConditions: You produced five clearly distinct poses.
Each pose remains readable when reduced to a black silhouette.
stretchGoals: Fix the weakest silhouette and re-test it.
reflectionPrompt: Which pose collapsed in silhouette, and what was hiding the problem?

title: Walk Cycle Fixer
summary: Diagnose and repair a broken walk cycle.
description: Take a walk cycle that feels wrong, yours or a starter one, and find the actual fault: foot slide, missing weight shift, dead hips, floaty contact. Fix one thing at a time and watch after each change.
deliverables: Before and after recordings plus a written list of the faults you found.
victoryConditions: You wrote down each fault you diagnosed before changing anything.
You fixed the faults one at a time and reviewed after each change.
stretchGoals: Make the same character walk as if it were exhausted.
reflectionPrompt: Which fault were you blind to until you slowed the playback down?

title: Impact Lab
summary: Make one hit land using sound, timing, and a single frame of hold.
description: Impact is craft, not volume. Take a collision and sell it: a frame or two of hold, a well-chosen sound, a touch of shake. Then remove each ingredient in turn and see which one was actually doing the work.
deliverables: A short clip of one impact plus versions with each ingredient removed.
victoryConditions: The finished impact uses sound, timing, and motion together.
You produced test versions with each ingredient removed to compare.
stretchGoals: Sell the same impact using sound alone.
reflectionPrompt: Which ingredient mattered least, and did that surprise you?

title: Fog & Depth
summary: Use atmosphere to separate layers instead of moving the camera.
description: Take a flat-looking frame and give it depth without changing the composition: atmospheric haze, falloff, a difference in contrast between layers. The subject should pop forward without being moved.
deliverables: Before and after renders of the same composition.
victoryConditions: The composition and camera are identical in both versions.
The subject separates from the background in the second version.
stretchGoals: Push it too far on purpose, then dial back to the point it reads best.
reflectionPrompt: How little atmosphere did you actually need before it read?

title: Trailer Cut
summary: Sell a story in thirty seconds without spoiling its ending.
description: Cut a trailer for something you have already made or something you like. Build interest, imply the shape of the story, and stop before the answer. Trailers are an exercise in what you leave out.
deliverables: A thirty-second trailer cut.
victoryConditions: The trailer runs at or under thirty seconds.
It creates interest without revealing how the story resolves.
stretchGoals: Cut a fifteen-second version that keeps the hook.
reflectionPrompt: Which shot were you most tempted to include, and why was leaving it out right?

title: One-Shot Challenge
summary: Tell a complete story in a single unbroken take.
description: No cuts. Everything has to be solved in camera: blocking, timing, reveals, the ending. One unbroken take forces you to plan properly, because there is nowhere to hide in the edit.
deliverables: One unbroken take that tells a complete story.
victoryConditions: The finished piece contains no cuts of any kind.
The story reaches an ending within the single take.
stretchGoals: Do it again and cut the length in half.
reflectionPrompt: What did you have to plan that an edit would normally have rescued?

title: Polish Pass
summary: Take something finished and fix ten small things.
description: Open an old finished piece and hunt for ten small faults: a frame too long, a level too hot, a title a pixel off, a cut that lands early. Fix them all. Polish is the difference between student work and professional work.
deliverables: The revised piece and the list of ten fixes you made.
victoryConditions: You found and wrote down ten specific faults before fixing them.
You applied all ten fixes and exported the revised version.
stretchGoals: Find ten more and decide which ones are genuinely worth doing.
reflectionPrompt: How many of the ten were invisible to you when you first called it finished?

title: Edit From Silence
summary: Cut a scene with the audio muted, then judge it with sound on.
description: Mute everything and cut the scene purely on picture. Then unmute and watch. You will find out how much of your usual rhythm comes from the sound rather than from the images.
deliverables: The silent cut and your notes after hearing it with sound.
victoryConditions: You completed the entire first cut with the audio muted.
You wrote down what changed in your judgement once sound was restored.
stretchGoals: Recut it with sound on and compare the two versions.
reflectionPrompt: Did the silent cut hold up, or was the sound carrying your timing?
